name: Bambu Lab (Shenzhen Tuozhu Technology)
origin_detail: Founded August 2020 in Shenzhen by four engineers led by Ye Tao, former head of DJI's consumer drone department; launched with the X1 Kickstarter (2022); offices in Shanghai and Austin, Texas.
openness_notes: Hardware designs and printer firmware are proprietary. The only open component is the slicer, Bambu Studio, licensed AGPL-3.0 because it is based on Prusa's PrusaSlicer (itself from Slic3r); its networking plugin is 'based on non-free libraries'. In January 2025 Bambu announced firmware with an authorization/authentication layer that gated third-party control of its printers behind its own software (Bambu Connect), a practical closing of interfaces rather than a licence change. Level 1 throughout; the date of the first public Bambu Studio source release was not verified.

relicensing_events.from: printers controllable over LAN/cloud by third-party tools
relicensing_events.to: firmware authorization/authentication architecture routing control through Bambu software (Bambu Connect)
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Users feared cloud authorization for LAN printing and restrictions on third-party slicers; Bambu edited the original post and called concerns misinformation; Louis Rossmann criticised unannounced terms-of-service changes. Whether the change was later reversed was not established in the sources reached.

risk_events: 2023-08: Bambu Cloud outage caused some printers to print uncontrollably or stop working
2024-08: Stratasys sued Bambu Lab for patent infringement
2025-01: firmware authorization controversy over third-party software access and terms-of-service changes
2025: security vulnerability found in the printers' cloud connection
robustness: Fast-growing and product-prolific (H2D, H2S, H2C in 2025; X2D, A2L, R1 laser and H3C in 2026) with a first flagship retail store in Shenzhen (Sept 2025), but customers depend on a single vendor's cloud and firmware; the 2023 cloud outage and 2025 vulnerability show that dependence. Patent litigation from Stratasys is an open exposure.
physical_science_relevance: Widely adopted fast multi-material printers are now common in labs, but closed firmware and cloud-gated control make them harder to integrate into automated, audited lab workflows than open printers.
openness_effect_assessment: Bambu Lab grew from a 2020 founding to market leadership while keeping hardware and firmware closed; its only open asset is an AGPL slicer it inherited from Prusa's open PrusaSlicer. Its success, which Josef Prusa blamed in 2025 for making open desktop hardware unviable, suggests that in this market closed, vertically integrated, venture-backed design and pricing beat openness, with openness benefiting Bambu as a free input rather than a strategy.
key_takeaway: Bambu Lab is the closed comparator that won: a DJI-alumni, VC-backed (IDG Capital) Shenzhen firm that reused open slicer code, kept printers and firmware proprietary, and in January 2025 tightened control further with authorization firmware, accepting a community backlash. Its rise is the main competitive force behind open pioneers' retreat (Prusa) and shows the 'open software, closed hardware' pattern at its most commercially effective.
